scope: The trusted overlap-trip predicate, trusted-clear predicate, adapter reconciliation and clock-fault latch retention around an externally computed base guard result. Not the base latch/slew algorithm or full native pedal controller.
semantics: trusted_overlap_trip requires exact input/config/state types, an ordinary Boolean prior latch, ordinary Boolean brake/comms/sensor flags all true, ordinary finite numeric policy with rise>0 and 0<=clear<trip<=1, and ordinary finite accelerator in[0,1] at or above trip.
External interlock and dt are deliberately absent from that narrow overlap-trip predicate; an early allocator or interlock fault can still retain a trusted missed trip.

trusted_clear_cycle requires normal candidate type/status(ok or saturated), exact input type, ordinary true Boolean comms/sensor/interlock, normal result type/status(ok or limited). It is a narrow predicate, not full candidate/result validation or signal provenance.
First adapter forces a trusted missed trip to latched+inhibited and preserves the base reason, falling back to brake_accelerator_overlap only when no reason exists.
Second adapter vetoes a prior-true to proposed-false transition unless trusted_clear_cycle holds; it forces latched+inhibited and preserves base reason, falling back to untrusted_overlap_latch_clear.
Clock faults additionally retain a prior true latch; they do not undo a newly observed conservative trip. Clock inhibition of final commands remains the separate native clock/final gate's ownership.
The base guard can itself trip its latch before a later communication/sensor inhibit. Adapters preserve that existing base result; do not silently redefine every trip as trusted.

C supports ordinary binary64 numbers, exact byte type/Boolean/status tags and valid Boolean base-proposed latches. It produces adapter action/latch/reason metadata only; it cannot independently authorize or generate positive torque.

Invalid C prior/proposed latch tags, clock tags and null required inputs fail closed with a veto and conservative true latch. These are explicit ABI guard extensions, not parity claims for impossible base-guard outputs.
Full allocation/output validation, base guard generation, pedal-source attestation, slew and signal mapping remain external obligations. The narrow predicates alone never certify a command.

planned_validation.oracle: Compare compiled predicates against unchanged Python helpers and adapter metadata against the real base-guard -> overlap -> trusted-clear -> clock-retention chain.
planned_validation.coverage: Threshold nextafter boundaries, malformed/nonnumeric scalars, every Boolean/type/status byte, early allocator/config/input faults, comms/sensor/interlock trust combinations, prior latch transitions, clock-invalid clear attempts and deterministic stateful sequences.
planned_validation.zero_acceptance: Whenever native adapter vetoes, apply an exact-zero inhibited guard before the existing C clock/final gate. Every held composed command must be exact positive zero; verify original clock-latch counterexamples and healthy low-pedal recovery.
planned_validation.domains: No custom Python numeric conversion hooks, unbounded diagnostic identifiers or malformed native pointers. Finite fixed-size native storage and explicit version; no byte-tag coercion.
planned_validation.repetition: Repeat a finite source-hashed compiled experiment deterministically; preserve prior PR heads and receipts.
planned_validation.review: Independent practical source review and adversarial probes at a stable checkpoint before draft PR.
planned_validation.excluded: No full base guard/slew/allocator port, actual APPS/BPPS attestation, firmware, CAN, target timing, hardware, HIL or safety approval.
